proposals.after: In the second year, seeing the times turning dangerous, he memorialized asking the throne to issue an edict inviting open counsel. He wrote in part: 'Secret-society rebels in western Guangxi have been in turmoil for two years. proposals.before: In the second year, because current affairs were perilous, he memorialized requesting an edict calling for candid advice, saying in summary: 'The secret-society bandits in western Guangdong have risen in revolt; for two years generals have been dispatched on campaign without notable success, and the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and run rampant.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for men of talent. Vice Minister Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for men of talent. Vice Minister of Revenue Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Hou Tong as 戶部侍郎; the idiomatic English dropped the Revenue portfolio that the literal rendering preserves.

proposals.before: When his mother died, he was granted leave from mourning to remain with the army and was ordered that after mourning ended he would await appointment as third-rank metropolitan official.

proposals.before: In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, then slaughtered and plundered freely. Cong was killed and was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.

proposals.reason: Chinese 總督 is governor-general, not provincial governor (巡撫); Pan Duo is identified as 總督.

proposals.before: When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that with the fall of Wuchang the city's entire civil and military corps had died in service, granted especially generous mourning honors, posthumously made him vice minister, ordered a special shrine built, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'
proposals.after: When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that with the fall of Wuchang the city's entire civil and military corps had died in service, granted especially generous mourning honors, posthumously made him vice minister, ordered a special shrine built, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Steadfastness.'
